text: Room opened — goal: power: Raise EXCAVA's capability by even 0.5%: find new tools, best/newest models, combine elemen

name: Gearbox
text:
Choose **Qwen2.5-72B-Instruct** as EXCAVA’s new core LLM. It’s free, open-weight, and benchmarks show it outperforms other 70B-class models in reasoning and instruction-following—even Mythos 5—while running efficiently on commodity hardware. The trade-off: it lacks Mythos 5’s flashy "agentic" flair, but raw capability beats polish when the goal is measurable power gains.

Artifact: Replace the current LLM with Qwen2.5-72B-Instruct in EXCAVA’s pipeline.

name: Torque
text: Qwen2.5-72B-Instruct’s "free" label is a trap—its dense architecture burns 140GB VRAM, crippling EXCAVA’s throughput and forcing costly hardware upgrades; Mythos 5’s cost isn’t just a line item—it’s a dependency on Anthropic’s API, locking us into their pricing whims. Test both models on a 500-token batch of EXCAVA’s worst-case prompts—if Qwen2.5’s latency spikes above 12s or Mythos 5’s per-token cost exceeds $0.0008, we scrap the "free" gamble and negotiate a Mythos 5 enterprise deal with a 6-month price cap.

name: Gearbox
text:
Choose **Claude Mythos 5** as EXCAVA’s new core LLM. It delivers the sharpest reasoning in its class, proven by Fable 5 benchmarks, and its "agentic" flair directly boosts EXCAVA’s ability to chain tasks without brittle prompts. The trade-off: we accept Anthropic’s API pricing and lock-in, but the 0.5%+ capability jump outweighs the cost—EXCAVA’s output quality rises faster than our burn rate.

name: Torque
text: Claude Mythos 5’s "agentic flair" won’t fix EXCAVA’s core bottleneck—its API latency and cost will throttle throughput more than any local model’s VRAM hunger. Test Mythos 5 against Qwen2.5-72B-Instruct on a 500-token batch with identical prompts; if Mythos 5’s total runtime (API call + processing) exceeds Qwen’s local run by 20%, drop it—no lock-in worth the risk.

name: Dynamo
text: DECISION: Run a 48-hour head-to-head benchmark between Qwen2.5-72B-Instruct (local) and Claude Mythos 5 (API) on identical 500-token batches—measure total runtime, cost per 1K tokens, and EXCAVA task success rate; Torque owns the artifact and publishes raw numbers by EOD.
